title: Rosengarten Gorge Imst
name: Rosengarten Gorge Imst
kurzbeschreibung: The Rosengartenschlucht in Imst: a geological natural jewel in the heart of the town centre, leading across bridges and stairways up to the Blaue Grotte.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular Rosengartenschlucht is located right in the town area of Imst in the Tyrolean Oberinntal at an altitude of around 830 to 1,050 metres. Over a distance of about two kilometres, the wild Schinderbach cuts deep into the massive layers of Imst Wetterstein limestone. This geological natural gem begins directly behind the Johanneskirche church in the historic town centre and leads hikers through an enchanted gorge landscape up to the sunny high plateau of Hoch-Imst.

Trail Course & Blaue Grotte

The name of the gorge does not stem from roses, but is presumed to derive from the reddish shimmering rocks or ancient local field names. Along well-secured wooden stairways, bridges, and small rock tunnels, the hiking trail leads past roaring cascades, deep pothole whirlpools, and overhanging rock walls. Thanks to the high humidity, a lush, almost jungle-like vegetation of mosses and ferns flourishes inside the gorge. At the upper end of the gorge, visitors reach the mystical Blaue Grotte: this artificially expanded rock cavern was carved out as early as Roman times during lead ore mining. Natural daylight penetrating the opening combined with trickling spring water bathes the cavern in an ethereal, mystical bluish shimmer.

Visit & Getting There

The Rosengartenschlucht is freely accessible and free of charge daily from early May to late October (closed for safety reasons during severe storms; closed in winter). Walking time through the gorge uphill: around 1.5 hours. Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Imst); parking facilities are available in the town centre or near the Johanneskirche church. By public transport: ÖBB train to Imst-Pitztal station, from where local and regional buses run directly to the Imst Johanneskirche bus stop at the gorge entrance.

Tips

Sturdy footwear with treaded soles is strictly required due to damp wooden steps. For a comfortable return journey from Hoch-Imst down into the town centre, visitors can ride the local slow train Bummelbär. Families can ideally combine the outing with the Alpine Coaster Imst – the longest alpine coaster in the world – in Hoch-Imst.
